note: Advanced Page Expiration (APE) gives per-path and per-status-code control of the Cache-Control max-age header. Settings live in the ape.settings config object: alternatives (path list), exclusions (path list denied caching), lifetime.alternatives, lifetime.301, lifetime.302, lifetime.404 (ints); the global default is core system.performance cache.page.max_age. Admin form at /admin/config/development/performance/ape (route ape.admin, permission 'administer ape', form id ape_settings). Behaviour is applied by ApeSubscriber (KernelEvents::RESPONSE priority -1024) which writes 'public, max-age=N' on cacheable responses, with status overrides (301/302/404 use their lifetimes, 403 forced to 0), and by the ExcludePages page_cache_response_policy. Extension points: ape_cache_set() (pre-set an age, used by Rules) and hook_ape_cache_alter(&$max_age,$original). No default ape.settings ships. Medium/hard cases are grounded in real ape.settings config: introspection reads a live lifetime/exclusion; execution sets the 404 lifetime and adds an excluded path, verified against live ape.settings config.

evals.prompt: The Drupal ape (Advanced Page Expiration) module controls the Cache-Control max-age header. Where do you configure it (route/path), which config object stores its settings, and what permission guards the admin form?
evals.expected_output: Configure it at /admin/config/development/performance/ape (route ape.admin, permission 'administer ape'). Its settings are stored in the ape.settings config object (the global default lifetime stays in system.performance cache.page.max_age).

evals.prompt: With the ape module, how do I give 301 redirects, 302 redirects and 404 responses their own cache lifetimes, and what happens to a 403 response's cache time? Name the config keys.
evals.expected_output: Set ape.settings lifetime.301, lifetime.302 and lifetime.404 (seconds) for those status codes; a 403 response is always forced to max-age 0 (never cached) by ApeSubscriber.

evals.prompt: In the ape module, how can I (a) stop specific paths from being cached at all, and (b) programmatically change the computed max-age from custom code?
evals.expected_output: (a) Add the paths to ape.settings 'exclusions' (enforced by the ExcludePages page_cache_response_policy, which denies caching). (b) Implement hook_ape_cache_alter(&$max_age, $original_max_age), or pre-set a value with ape_cache_set().

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, ape is configured. Inspect the live ape.settings configuration and report the cache lifetime (in seconds) that ape applies to 404 Not Found responses.
On this Drupal site, ape is configured to exclude certain paths from page caching. Inspect the live ape.settings configuration and name a path that is excluded from caching.
evals.expected_output: ape.settings exclusions lists /ape_exclude and /user/* — those paths are excluded from page caching.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the ape module to set the cache lifetime for 404 Not Found responses to 300 seconds (5 minutes). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: ape.settings lifetime.404 is 300 (e.g. \Drupal::configFactory()->getEditable('ape.settings')->set('lifetime.404', 300)->save(), or set it on the APE settings form).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the ape module to exclude the path /ape_exclude from page caching (add it to APE's list of excluded pages). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: ape.settings 'exclusions' contains /ape_exclude (one path per line), so the ExcludePages policy denies caching for it.
